I think that might be a tell-all, Congressman.
Your thoughts on Dr. Fauci yesterday?
It certainly seems to be, Addison, a tell, because if you have nothing to hide, you would
just say, I'm not getting any royalties at all, and here's my financial record.
Right.
But for some weird reason, he won't do that.
But what Fauci has done, and the CDC really, they mixed politics with medicine for over
two years.
And when you do that, you get two results.
You get bad politics, and then you get bad medicine.
And we saw it with very inconsistent guidance.
They were saying, like, when people were protesting the lockdowns, and having Americans being told
they weren't essential, they were saying, oh, you're spreading COVID.
They were saying, oh, you're a super spreader.
But when the left wanted to protest George Floyd, they said, oh, that's perfectly fine.
Just wear a mask.
That doesn't make any sense.
And we all know that natural immunity is the best immunity.
And for them to say that you should also, I mean, when I got COVID, I almost died of it
in February 2020.
My infectious disease doctor specifically told me, do not get the vaccine for six months.
You don't need it.
It's not going to do you any good.
It's just going to make you sick.
Yeah, yeah, that's right.
And I have a family friend who's a doctor and prescribed, was prescribing things like ivermectin
to people with COVID because it worked.
Because it worked.
My father, I don't know if he's going to kill me or not for saying this, he took ivermectin
when he had COVID.
The next day, it was a night and day difference.
Nothing else worked.
He took ivermectin night and day difference for him.
And what were we told by the regime, by Fauci, by the NIH and the World Health Organization?
Ivermectin is horse-paced.
Don't take ivermectin.
Why did they not want us to take ivermectin, Congressman?
It's because it would keep you out of the hospital.
You didn't have to pay up that big hospital bill because they were going to pump you full
of big pharma's chemicals.
Well, you know what?
Ivermectin, how about hydrochloroquine?
We had a physician in Texas, Robin Armstrong, who prescribed it to 65 patients in a nursing
home that had COVID and not one of them passed away.
Not one of them.
And these are nursing homes, very vulnerable folks, all 65.
That is not anecdotal.
That is scientific.
But also, you know, the antibody, the monoclonal antibodies.
So we've treated it.
COVID is over.
For them to say now that, oh, we're about to defeat it.
We defeated it.
There's treatments for it.

American people.

I don't know.
Yeah.
Yeah, it is.
It is absolutely criminal.

bureaucracy.

from COVID.
But they were focused on lining big pharma's pockets instead.
Congressman Pat Fallon, a pleasure to have you on the show.
Thank you so much for joining.
I appreciate it.
Thanks, Addison.
God bless.
Thanks, Addison.
God bless.
Joining us now to continue the conversation, we're bringing in former CIA cover operations
officer Mike Baker and former U.S. Deputy military representative to NATO General Blaine Holt.
Great to have both of you with us.
Thank you.
All right.
General Holt, I want to start with you.
What do you make of the relationship between Chinese President Xi and Vladimir Putin?
Is it a close relationship or is there actually something going on behind the scenes that we might not
know about?
Are they as close as we're guessing they are?
So to use a Facebook term, it's complicated.
The trouble is no Russian-China marriage ever survived.
They've all gone to divorce court.
And this one will head that way too eventually.
But right now, both these guys, Xi and Putin, they need each other.
Putin has got to go find material and monetary support for his war.
Xi Jinping has got to just destroy wrecked economy and he's trying to get reconfirmed next month.
He's got to get cheap Russian oil and pipeline deals.
So they need each other.
But they also have strategic designs.
And I'm sure Mike will have more to say about that.
Yeah. All right.
Mike, your take on the Xi-Putin relationship.
Yeah, the general is absolutely right.
Look, it's got a long track record of, you know, in and out here.
You know, they occasionally are best friends and then they're not.
And it's entirely dependent on Xi's self-interest and China's self-interest.
China, the regime, does nothing that isn't in their perceived best interest.
Now, Russia does the same thing.
And you could argue a lot of countries do.
And you could argue the U.S. is the only one that apologizes when we do act in our own best interest.
But with Xi, he's driving this dance right now.
You know, Putin needs Xi more than Xi needs Putin, I would argue, at this stage.
But we shouldn't read too much into this.
This is all about self-interest.
Right now, it's in both their interests to team up.
It's in both their interests to view this as a way to kick the U.S. in the backside.
And that's always of interest to both of these nations.
Yeah. And, you know, General Holt, with regards to Vladimir Putin, I mean, he's so, I would say, kind of like a lone wolf type.
And I mean, I can't imagine that his country now seeing the disastrous way that the war in Ukraine is going would support him much longer.
Do you have any insight into the future for Putin?
Yep. So it's definitely true that his circle is shrinking around him.
And it's very doubtful that he's ever getting very accurate information about what's going on in the war.
One place, though, that we shouldn't be so quick to say that, oh, Russia's finished.
He knows that he has a full house in his hand with regards to the energy crisis that is now foisted from these sanctions in Europe.
We've already seen five governments fall.
And yet Ursula von der Leyen and the current leaders, Liz Truss, they're doubling down on this strategy of we're going to get off Russian gas by the end of the year.
But but so no one should think that Putin's in any way, shape or form finished.
He's just very much weakened and he's in trouble and he knows it.
And, you know, and Mike, as you pointed out, that you think Putin definitely needs Xi way more than Xi needs Putin.
I want to switch a little bit, though, to Taiwan here and get your reaction to this, Mike.
Chinese president, of course, Xi told his military that he wants to have the capability to take control of Taiwan by force by 2027.
Now, this is per CIA deputy director David Cohen, who said that he does not currently believe that Beijing has made a decision about whether or not to proceed.
Your take on this.
Yeah, I think they've definitely accelerated their timeline.
You know, I agree with the assessment they haven't picked a date on the calendar, but that's a you know, that's that's such a logistical issue.

I think that what they're seeing in the world and the way that they assess it, meaning the Chinese regime right now, I think they have definitely pushed up this concept of of, you know, we want to bring Taiwan back into the fold.
Look, the question that they ask themselves every time they look at this as a as a as a plan, as a scenario is, you know, what will be the pushback?
You know, what's going to happen, particularly from the U.S. and our allies if they do make a move on Taiwan?
And so they have to look at real world scenarios.
And, you know, it's not a theoretical exercise.
They look at what's happened in Ukraine and they looked at, you know, it's its its sanctions.
We've said the red line is boots on the ground.
Now, the Chinese regime sits and they stare at each other across their conference table and they say, do we think there would be any difference if we move on Taiwan?
Meaning, do we think that the president, whether it's Biden or the next administration, would say, OK, we are putting boots on the ground to defend Taiwan?
And that's at the end of the day. I don't want to oversimplify this.
But that is the base calculation that they make.
Yeah. So it sounds like they're they're kind of hedging a little bit, trying to say, you know, will they or won't they?
They being the United States. General Holt, before we go, I would love to get your thoughts on China invading Taiwan with force.
Will it happen? Won't it happen?
I just think they get hurt too badly and they're not going to do that right now.
Certainly on this side of October 16th, which is the 20th Congress that's supposed to confirm Xi, they're not going to do anything.
And I would also argue that Xi and the CCP has a much higher goal and it involves the BRICS and it involves disintermediating or getting rid of the U.S. dollar on world markets.
And right now they've got a lot of fans that we should be very worried about in Saudi Arabia, Turkey and India.
We have to watch those very carefully. Wow. OK.
I'd say that the generalist had one more point, which is that I think there's also an emotive issue here.
And by that, I mean, Xi doesn't want to leave the world stage.
He's not going to give up until he has reunified with Taiwan.
So based on his health, whatever, he's definitely getting a third term out of this Congress coming up next month at the general mention.
But that is a calculation that we have to play into as well.
He is not leaving the world stage, would be my assessment, without bringing Taiwan back into the fold.
Our world today is undergoing accelerating changes unseen in a century.
And it has entered a new phase of uncertainty and transformation.
It is important for us to ride down the trend of the times, strengthen solidarity and cooperation,
and build a closer SCO community with a shared future.
First, we need to enhance mutual support.
We should support each other in our efforts to uphold security and development interests,
and guard against attempts by external forces to instigate colour revolutions,
